datasets.title: Macrophages protect against sensory axon degeneration in diabetic neuropathy
datasets.summary: Diabetic peripheral neuropathy (DPN) is a common complication of diabetes, causing sensory loss and debilitating neuropathic pain1,2. Although the onset and progression of DPN have been linked with dyslipidemia and hyperglycemia3, the contribution of inflammation in the pathogenesis of DPN has not been investigated. Here, we use a High Fat High Fructose Diet (HFHFD) to model DPN and its metabolic syndrome in mice. Diabetic mice develop persistent heat hypoalgesia after three months, but a reduction in epidermal skin innervation only manifests at 6 months. Using single-cell sequencing, we find that CCR2+ macrophages infiltrate the sciatic nerves of diabetic mice well before axonal degeneration is detectable. We show that these infiltrating macrophages share gene expression similarities with nerve crush-induced macrophages4 and express neurodegeneration-associated microglia marker genes5 although there is no axon loss or demyelination yet. Inhibiting this macrophage recruitment in diabetic mice by genetically or pharmacologically blocking CCR2 signaling results in a more severe heat hypoalgesia and accelerated skin denervation. These findings reveal a novel neuroprotective recruitment of macrophages into peripheral nerves of diabetic mice that delays the onset of terminal axonal degeneration, thereby reducing sensory loss. Potentiating and sustaining this early neuroprotective immune response in patients represents, therefore, a potential means to reduce or prevent DPN.

datasets.overall_design: We fed male C57Bl6 mice on a high fat high fructose diet (HFHFD) or control diet (CD) for 12 weeks. Mice fed HFHFD become diabetic. datasets.title: Dorsal root ganglion single-cell RNA-seq dataset of painful diabetic peripheral neuropathy rat, diabeitc rats, and health rats
datasets.summary: Painful diabetic peripheral neuropathy (PDPN) is a common complication of diabetes mellitus (DM).   As one of the most disturbing symptoms, mechanical allodynia (MA) in PDPN remains largely unexplored. This dataset contains single-cell RNA sequencing results from rat dorsal root ganglion (DRG). The goal of this experiment was to investigate the transcriptional changes of distinct cell types in the DRG along MA development.
datasets.overall_design: Diabetic rats were induced by injected streptozotocin (STZ) on Day 0. We grouped diabetic rats according to the 50% paw withdrawal threshold (PWT) on Day 28. Rats with PWT ≤ 8 g were selected into the PDPN group and rats with PWT ≥ 15g were selected into the DM group. Rats in normal group (N group) were injected vehicle on Day 0. This experiment contains 8 samples (4 PDPN, 2 DM and 2 N), each of which combined bilateral L5 DRG collected from one male rat.

datasets.title: Single cell sequencing datasets of tibial nerves from diabetic neuropathy (DPN) patients and traumatic limb amputation (TLA) patients.
datasets.summary: To understand the cellular diversity and alterations in the pathogenesis of diabetic neuropathy (DPN), weenrolled 4 DPN patients, 3 traumatic limb amputation (TLA) patients at the Department of Orthopedic Surgery of Shanghai Sixth People’s Hospital, Shanghai, China.
datasets.overall_design: Tibial nerves were collected during amputation surgeries in patients suffering from diabetic peripheral neuropathy (DPN) or patients with traumatic limb amputation (TLA). Nerve samples isolated from TLA patients were set as control group. Tibial nerves from donors were rapidly frozen on liquid nitrogen in the operating room and stored until tissue digestion. The sequencing data for 4 DPN samples were named as "DPN_Sample 1-4" and the sequencing data for 3 TLA samples were named as "TLA_Sample 1-3".

datasets.summary: Diabetic peripheral neuropathy (DPN) is the most common form of neuropathy, and have considerable morbidity, which occurs in approximately 50% of diabetic patients. Here, we performed scRNA-seq technology using 10× Genomics sequencing on DRG tissues isolated from control and DPN rats, to identify the cell type composition of DRG, and to reveal the roles of different cell types in mediating DPN.
